questions.q: England is ___ than Egypt.
questions.explanation: When comparing two things, we use the comparative form: 'more expensive'.

questions.q: Oh dear, I ___ a terrible headache!
questions.explanation: 'Have got' is correct with the first-person pronoun 'I'. It expresses possession.

questions.q: The firemen think ___ cigarette started the fire.
questions.explanation: 'A' is the correct indefinite article before 'cigarette' (consonant sound).

questions.q: My father is writing a book ___ his life.
questions.explanation: 'About' is used to indicate the subject matter of a book.

questions.q: I ___ a can and broke two toes on my left foot.
questions.explanation: 'Dropped' (simple past) describes a completed action in the past.

questions.q: France is bigger ___ England.
questions.explanation: Comparative adjectives are followed by 'than': 'bigger than'.

questions.q: You ___ over 15 to watch this movie.
questions.explanation: 'Have to be' expresses a requirement with the second-person subject 'you'.

questions.q: Her mother said she ___ to the disco with her friends.
questions.explanation: In reported speech, 'can' becomes 'could'. So 'could go' is correct.

questions.q: I think he is ___ thin. He looks sick.
questions.explanation: 'Too' is used before adjectives to express excess: 'too thin'.

questions.q: You must ___ before you turn left or right.
questions.explanation: After modal verbs like 'must', we use the base form of the verb: 'must signal'.

questions.q: It's quite cloudy today, but I don't think it ___ rain.
questions.explanation: 'Will' is used for predictions or opinions about the future, especially with 'I don't think'.

questions.q: At 5 o'clock, we ___ still for the bus.
questions.explanation: Past continuous ('were waiting') describes an action in progress at a specific past time.

questions.q: When ___ you last ___ a photograph?
questions.explanation: Simple past questions use 'did' + base form of the verb: 'When did you last take'.

questions.q: The house is very dark because it ___ very small windows.
questions.explanation: 'Hasn't got' is the correct negative for third-person singular ('the house'). It means the house lacks large windows.

questions.q: I met my best friend ___ university.
questions.explanation: We use 'at' with institutions: 'at university', 'at school'.

questions.q: I am ___ today than I was yesterday.
questions.explanation: 'Happier' is the comparative form of 'happy', used when comparing two states.

questions.q: George Clooney is one ___ famous actors in the world.
questions.explanation: The correct superlative structure is 'one of the most + adjective + plural noun'.

questions.q: I'm not enjoying ___ film. Let's go home.
questions.explanation: 'This' refers to something currently being experienced, like a film being watched right now.

questions.q: I'm twenty, but I've ___ been in love.
questions.explanation: 'Never' is the negative adverb used with the present perfect to mean 'not at any time'.

questions.q: The weather today is ___ than yesterday.
questions.explanation: 'Better' is the irregular comparative form of 'good'. 'Gooder' and 'more good' are incorrect.

questions.q: I ___ make you a chocolate cake for your birthday.
questions.explanation: 'Am going to' expresses a future intention or plan with the first-person singular subject.

questions.q: Did your mother make you ___ hat?
questions.explanation: 'That' is the singular demonstrative pronoun used to point to a specific item.

questions.q: Are you going out ___?
questions.explanation: We say 'this evening' without any preposition.

questions.q: I ___ she was your sister, but now I know she's your wife.
questions.explanation: 'Thought' (simple past) is correct as the action of thinking happened in the past.

questions.q: I think American people are ___ than English people.
questions.explanation: 'Friendlier' is the correct comparative form of 'friendly' (adjectives ending in -y take -ier).

questions.q: If ___ later, so take an umbrella.
questions.explanation: After modal verbs like 'could', we use the base form of the verb: 'could rain'.

questions.q: How often ___ around here?
questions.explanation: 'Do they' is the correct auxiliary for forming frequency questions in the simple present with a plural subject.

questions.q: Digital cameras are good ___ you don't need a film.
questions.explanation: 'So' introduces a result or consequence: 'Digital cameras are good, so you don't need a film.'

questions.q: I'm going to the store ___ some food for tonight.
questions.explanation: 'To buy' (infinitive of purpose) explains the reason for going to the store.

questions.q: I like my house, ___ the garden isn't very nice.
questions.explanation: 'But' expresses contrast between two ideas.

questions.q: We were all afraid when we ___ the terrible noise.
questions.explanation: 'Heard' (simple past) describes a completed action in the past.

questions.q: I wear 2 earrings in ___ ear.
questions.explanation: 'Each' refers to every individual item considered separately: 'each ear' (left and right).

questions.q: You ___ home now children - it's three o'clock.
questions.explanation: 'Can go' is correct. After modal verbs like 'can', we use the bare infinitive.

questions.q: We used ___ brick to break the window.
questions.explanation: 'A' is the correct indefinite article before 'brick' (consonant sound), referring to one unspecified brick.

questions.q: Sharon ___ an older brother called Reg.
questions.explanation: 'Has got' is correct for the third-person singular subject 'Sharon'.

questions.q: You don't ___ make dinner tonight.
questions.explanation: 'Don't have to' means there is no obligation. 'Don't must' is grammatically incorrect.

questions.q: It's one of the biggest ___ I've ever seen.
questions.explanation: After 'one of the biggest', the noun must be plural: 'towns'.

questions.q: They're ___ their friend's house for dinner.
questions.explanation: 'At' is used with specific locations: 'at their friend's house'.

questions.q: In 1999, we ___ in a small house in Bristol.
questions.explanation: With a specific past time reference ('In 1999') and subject 'we', 'were living' (past continuous) describes a situation in progress at that past time.
